problem_statement: A new file system is needed for the Native Simulator that mounts a host directory into Zephyr's file system hierarchy, so that Zephyr can access and modify host files and folders as if they were an ordinary embedded mount point. The file system must support the full file system API (open, close, read, write, stat, statvfs, lseek, tell, truncate, sync, unlink, rename, mkdir, opendir, readdir, closedir) by forwarding operations to the host file system, and a mount point may be supplied via the -volume=HOST:ZEPHYR[:ro] command-line argument (optionally read-only).

verification.reason: The statement describes the feature but omits two public interface names that the hidden tests directly reference: the Kconfig option CONFIG_FILE_SYSTEM_NATIVE_MOUNT and the enum value FS_NATIVE_MOUNT. Both are addable to the statement without revealing implementation details.

problems.detail: The test's prj.conf enables CONFIG_FILE_SYSTEM_NATIVE_MOUNT=y and the test's mount.c sets .type = FS_NATIVE_MOUNT, but the problem statement never mentions either the Kconfig option name CONFIG_FILE_SYSTEM_NATIVE_MOUNT or the enum value FS_NATIVE_MOUNT that must be added to the filesystem type enum in fs.h.

problem_statement_fixed:
A new file system is needed for the Native Simulator that mounts a host directory into Zephyr's file system hierarchy, so that Zephyr can access and modify host files and folders as if they were an ordinary embedded mount point. The file system must be enabled by CONFIG_FILE_SYSTEM_NATIVE_MOUNT and registered under the file system type identifier FS_NATIVE_MOUNT in zephyr/fs/fs.h.

The file system must support the full file system API (open, close, read, write, stat, statvfs, lseek, tell, truncate, sync, unlink, rename, mkdir, opendir, readdir, closedir) by forwarding operations to the host file system. A mount point may be supplied via the -volume=HOST:ZEPHYR[:ro] command-line argument; the argument may be provided multiple times, each instance mounting one host directory at one Zephyr mount point. HOST may be an absolute or relative host path, and a trailing :ro makes the mount read-only. These -volume arguments must be processed automatically by the Native Simulator so that the mounted paths are available to application code without an explicit fs_mount(). Path components after the Zephyr mount point must be resolved by appending them to the host directory.

For a programmatic mount, a struct fs_mount_t should use .type = FS_NATIVE_MOUNT, .mnt_point as the Zephyr mount path, .fs_data as a pointer to the NUL-terminated host directory path, and .storage_dev = NULL. fs_mount() should succeed without a storage device or mkfs and should make the host directory available at .mnt_point. unlink must be able to remove both files and empty directories, since the file system API does not provide a separate directory-removal operation.
